findings.before: Both plots use a requested movement of Paul toward Jerusalem as an opportunity to kill him en route.
findings.after: Both plots use a requested transfer of Paul as an opportunity to kill him en route.
findings.fix: The earlier plot requests movement to the council from the barracks; do not turn it into a second intercity journey toward Jerusalem.
findings.resolution: Applied to the stable preview and confirmed in the final133-unit primary; original identities and counts are unchanged.

findings.before: The later narrative supplies its own eight-or-ten-day stay and next-day hearing rather than an independent measure of soon.
findings.after: The later narrative states a stay of no more than eight or ten days and a hearing the day after his descent, rather than independently measuring soon.
findings.fix: Preserve the original upper-limit wording rather than converting it into an exact duration.
findings.resolution: Applied to the stable preview and confirmed in the final133-unit primary; original identities and counts are unchanged.

findings.before: The arrival of Agrippa and Bernice to greet Festus leads to their participation in the following day's hearing. Their repeated names establish the visitor-to-audience connection without supplying an unstated family or marital relationship.
findings.after: Agrippa and Bernice arrive to greet Festus and later participate in the hearing. The intervening account says they stayed several days, and the next-day hearing follows the promise in25:22, not an explicit day-after-arrival interval. Their repeated names establish the visitor-to-audience connection without adding a family or marital relationship.
findings.fix: Distinguish the visit lasting several days from tomorrow following Agrippa's hearing request.
findings.resolution: Applied to the stable preview and confirmed in the final133-unit primary; original identities and counts are unchanged.

findings.before: they are courteous speech openings in distinct hearings, not the same governor or audience.
findings.after: they are courteous speech openings in distinct hearings, addressing Agrippa the king and Felix the governor.
findings.fix: Do not suggest that Agrippa has the same governor title as Felix.
findings.resolution: Applied to the stable preview and confirmed in the final133-unit primary; original identities and counts are unchanged.

findings.before: The earlier narrative describes Saul obtaining the high priest's letters for Damascus and seeking to bind followers of the Way.
findings.after: The earlier narrative describes Saul requesting the high priest's letters for Damascus in order to bind followers of the Way.
findings.fix: Acts9:1–2 narrates a request for letters, not their actual granting in those retained units.
findings.resolution: Applied to the stable preview and confirmed in the final133-unit primary; original identities and counts are unchanged.
